summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and type 2 diabetes presented with acute substernal chest pain, bradycardia, and nausea after a shower. He was found to have severe hyperkalemia (K+ 6.7) with ECG changes including peaked T waves and first-degree AV block. He received emergency treatment with calcium gluconate, insulin, dextrose, sodium bicarbonate, and Kayexalate, followed by emergent hemodialysis. His potassium normalized, chest pain resolved, and ECG returned to baseline. Serial troponins were stable, indicating no acute myocardial infarction. He remained hemodynamically stable on telemetry, completed a scheduled dialysis session, and was discharged home in good condition with medication adjustments and dietary instructions to avoid high-potassium foods.
